tasks.title: Online privacy priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for a digital privacy framework
listItems: requiring explicit consent for every data use
giving users the right to delete all stored data
making privacy settings simple and accessible

promptBlocks.heading: Some opinions expressed in the discussion:
paragraphs: Explicit consent forces companies to be transparent. Without it, people agree to things they don't understand.
The right to deletion gives people real control. If you can't delete your data, you don't really own it.
Simple settings are the only way to protect the majority. Most people won't read long privacy policies.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more important for protecting online privacy, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Privacy awareness proposal
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Proposal for a digital privacy framework planning brief 19
paragraphs: The organisers of the Digital Privacy Framework Planning Brief 19 are considering launching a public awareness campaign to help residents understand their online privacy rights. The campaign would include workshops, online resources and local events. The organisers have invited proposals from community members for how this campaign should be designed.
Write a proposal for the organisers. In your proposal, you should:
• recommend two specific activities or resources the campaign should include
• explain how these activities would benefit residents and encourage responsible data practices
• suggest how the organisers could measure the campaign's effectiveness

tasks.title: Data-sharing concerns
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Your views on data-sharing requirements
paragraphs: As you know, the Digital Privacy Framework Planning Brief 19 is considering a proposal that would require all local businesses to obtain explicit consent before sharing customer data with third parties. Some business owners have expressed concern that this requirement will be burdensome and may reduce their ability to offer personalised services. Others argue it is essential for protecting consumer trust.

I would like to hear your views on this proposal. Please write back explaining your position on the proposed consent requirement, analysing one potential implication for small businesses, and proposing an action the planning brief could take to support businesses while still protecting privacy.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to the Programme Coordinator.

tasks.title: Privacy tool review
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Digital privacy tools
paragraphs: Have you used a digital privacy tool – for example, a password manager, a VPN, a browser extension that blocks trackers, or an app that helps you manage your online accounts?
We want to hear about your experience. Write a review of the tool for our community website.

Describe what the tool does and how easy it is to use. Evaluate how effectively it protects your privacy without making everyday tasks inconvenient. Would you recommend this tool to other residents? Why or why not?
The best reviews will be published on our website.
